newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambia to cut power export to Zimbabwe due drought.
newsitem.headline: Zambia to cut power export to Zimbabwe due drought.

text.p: Zambia may cut power to Zimbabwe by half by December in response to a drop in output resulting from prolonged drought, the state-run Zambia Electricity Supply Corp (ZESCO) said on Thursday.
"Unless people start saving power now, we will have no option but to cut our exports to Zimbabwe by 50 megawatts per month," ZESCO marketing manager Alex Matale told Reuters.

The export cut would be the second this year. In January, ZESCO reduced its power exports to Zimbabwe from 200 to 100 megawatts per month, translating into a $1 million loss in power earnings per month.
The corporation also started importing power from Zaire to meet a domestic shorfall.
"However, the Zaire line is now being fully utilised, and if our output drops further, we will have nowhere to import from," Matale said.
He said they were under long-term contractual obligations to export to Zimbabwe.
"We have to export to Zimbabwe in spite of our own shortfall to meet long-term contractual obligations," he said.
Recently ZESCO introduced a quota system under which a 50 percent surcharge is slapped on users who exceed the allocated quota.
Zambia has been experiencing a drought for over 10 years, resulting in diminished water levels at ZESCO's main reservoirs.
